Endometrial stromal sarcoma. Uniform, small, darkly staining cells are arranged in sheets and whorls around small vessels. This may be present in the abdomen and other soft tissue sites, especially in foci of endometriosis or as metastatic deposits. The lesional cells express CD10, ER (in nuclei), and sometimes cytokeratins focally. Some have a t(7;17)(p15;q21), with fusion of JAZF1 and SUZ12 genes, although this is less frequent in extrauterine examples. Recently a t(10;17)(q22;p13) variant was described, with YWHAE - FMA22A / B fusion; this has higher-grade morphology and manifests aggressive behavior

full.description: This is a micrograph showing a histologic section of endometrial stromal sarcoma. The image displays uniform, small, darkly staining cells arranged in sheets and whorls around small vessels. These neoplastic cells infiltrate the tissue in a characteristic pattern resembling proliferative endometrial stroma. The morphological features are indicative of endometrial stromal sarcoma, which can occur in the uterus or extrauterine sites.

random.description: This is a high-magnification photomicrograph of a lymph node stained with H&E. The section shows a dense population of small, monotonous lymphocytes replacing the normal architecture. These cytological and architectural features are characteristic of small lymphocytic lymphoma or chronic lymphocytic leukemia involving a lymph node.

Morphological spectrum of ductal prostate adenocarcinoma. (a) Large nodule of ductal adenocarcinoma showing endometrioid growth pattern with admixture of confluent cribriform and papillary patterns with irregular slit-like lumina and glands lined by tall columnar lining epithelium. (b) PIN-like ductal adenocarcinoma often has large well-formed glands lined by pseudostratified tall columnar cells, mimicking HGPIN. Large glandular architecture and tall columnar celllining distinguishes PIN-like ductal adenocarcinoma from conventional acinar cancer. Marked glandular crowding distinguishes it from HGPIN.
